open_questions: 1. FABLE 5's MARK IS `claude` (assets/logos/ai-models/claude-color.png), and that is a decision, not a fallback. LAW 35 wants the product mark over the company mark, and there is no 'Fable' asset in the registry or published anywhere - the Claude/Anthropic sunburst IS the mark of this model family, so it is the product mark here. If someone later registers a dedicated `fable` key, swap it. The three things that are never legal in its place: `claude-code` (the CLI mascot, a different product), `claude-code-sticker` (the die-cut sticker MARK IDENTITY retired), and a drawn wordmark or a text pill (LAW 2 / LAW 33).

2. 'ONE BENCHMARK' AND THE DOUBLE-CAPTION DETECTOR. The key is written at 5.40 while a pill carrying 'Now, this was for one specific benchmark,' is alive. The two strings are not identical and caption_identity_guard is an overlap test on identical text, so the guard passes - but a clerk reading by eye could call it an echo. If it does, the whiteboard author writes the disagreement to plans/kimifable_wb_notes.md and builds the plan as written; the sanctioned replacement, if Miguel ever rules on it, is THE BENCHMARK, because the picture (one terracotta row out of three) already carries the word 'one'. Dropping the key entirely is NOT an option: it would break the whiteboard's own LABEL LAW, which is the stronger law of the two.

3. 'FRONT-END DESIGN' IS WRITTEN AT 15.05 AND THE WINDOW IS 0.07 s WIDE. 'design,' starts at 14.12, LABEL_WINDOW is 1.0 s, so 15.12 is the last legal instant and 15.05 sits 70 ms inside it. It is late on purpose: a pill reading 'is fantastic as front-end design,' is alive until ~14.6 and printing the same words beside it is the LAW 4 echo. If the measured caption chunker moves that pill's end past 15.05, the fix is to shorten the KEY to FRONT-END and keep the time - never to move the key earlier into the pill, and never to shrink the LABEL_WINDOW.

4. THE '-66%' READOUT IS A DELTA, NOT A QUOTATION. He says 'cut your build by 66%.' and the board prints '-66%' inside the cost track as its value readout, one block with the track, ~900 px above the caption seam. It is not a verbatim pill string (the minus sign and the missing 'by' are the point) and it is the only numeral in the video. A counter lane that shows the number the claim is about is exactly what the lane exists for; it is recorded here so a clerk sees the reasoning instead of guessing at it.

5. PHONE TEST RISK - ANSWERED BY THE SEAL, 2026-09-08, and this entry is the record rather than an open question. All four objects were cut at 405x720 off the page and read blind by three independent rounds of one reader per crop, and the seal is review/artwork_pass_kimifable.json (PASS, 4 objects, 3 rounds). Results: 'a price tag' 3/3 'price tag' (2 sure); 'a benchmark scorecard' 3/3 'clipboard' (3 sure, scored SYNONYM - the reader names the same thing the picture is); 'a website layout' 3/3 'web browser window' / 'browser window' (3 sure, SYNONYM); 'a folder of designs' 3/3 'file folder' (3 sure). ZERO readers named a different object. Two of the four are NOT the drawing this plan's first draft specified, and the amendment record says why: a hung tag read 'birdhouse', and a stack of three windows could not be committed to because the instrument asks for THE SINGLE object. What survives as guidance for any later re-read: score the IDEA, not the noun - 'tag', 'label', 'luggage tag' pass for the tag; 'clipboard', 'scorecard', 'chart on a board' pass for the scorecard; 'browser window', 'web page', 'website' pass for the layout; 'folder', 'file folder', 'documents folder' pass for the folder. A DIFFERENT thing ('birdhouse', 'credit cards', 'receipt', 'calendar') or a hedge is a FAIL, and a fail is a redesign that must be re-sealed by production.py artwork-pass, never a label bolted on.

6. THE 1-of-3 RUNS THROUGH ALL FOUR CHAPTERS ON PURPOSE. One coin against three; one terracotta row of three; one tall bar of three; a cost bar cut back to just over a third. That repetition is the lane's argument and it is deliberate - it is not four devices saying the same thing (each is a different claim about a different quantity), and an author must not 'vary' it for visual interest.
